title: GDPR Data Retention Period: None Set, CNIL Guide Says 3 Years
meta_description: The GDPR fixes no retention period. The CNIL’s non-binding guide says non-customer prospect data may be kept 3 years from its collection or last contact.
secondary_keywords: how long can you keep prospect data

image.takeaway: No fixed GDPR period; a non-binding CNIL guide proposes 3 years for prospects from collection or last contact.
image.alt: Hero card for an article on the GDPR data retention period: the GDPR fixes none, and the CNIL’s non-binding guide proposes three years for a prospect who is not a customer, from collection or last contact.

rows.label: Fixed retention period in the GDPR text
rows.note: Article 5(1)(e): no longer than necessary in identifiable form

rows.label: CNIL framework: customer data used for prospecting

key_numbers.source: Read on 12 November 2026 from the EU GDPR on EUR-Lex, the ICO’s storage limitation and direct marketing guidance, the CNIL’s 2021 reference framework on Légifrance, and the CNIL’s KASPR releases of 19 December 2024 and 6 March 2026.
